assumptions.summary: The supplied review data are treated as true and reliable.
Only the provided date is used; external environment and Amazon internal evaluation are ignored.
Helpfulness, verified and Vine factors are used in the rating indicator.
Correlation and autocorrelation are used to select dynamic relationships.
PCA contribution is used to build a success index.
5% and 10% sentiment reductions are used as robustness checks.
The success index is used for timely product tracking.

source.title: Strategies to Online Sales: A Review-tracking System Combined with Deep Learning and Difference Equation Model

source_quality.summary: All 33 pages were read in physical order and visually reconciled. The scan exposes a substantive Summary Sheet and a raster body covering product lifecycle indicators, TF-IDF and BP sentiment, difference equations, PCA success indices, sensitivity, weaknesses and a dated marketing letter.

decisions: which review indicators to track, how ratings and sentiment interact, how next-quarter changes are bounded, which products/features deserve attention, and when to intervene using the success index

title: Strategies to Online Sales: A Review-tracking System Combined with Deep Learning and Difference Equation Model
unresolved_questions: The source data are assumed real and reliable without row-level provenance.
Only supplied dates are used, so external time effects are omitted.
External product-market conditions are ignored.
Amazon internal evaluation and supervision effects are ignored.
Cleaning rules and excluded records are not released as a ledger.
Quarter grouping may hide launch-season and calendar effects.
The five indicators are selected by authors rather than validated against an outcome.
Helpful, verified and Vine multipliers are not calibrated as trust probabilities.
The weighted rating equation may change ordinal meaning through heuristic factors.
The favorable-rate threshold is not independently justified.
Review count is not sales volume without exposure correction.
Average review words confound verbosity with information.
Sentiment values depend on the labeled training set and annotation quality.
Dictionary examples show failure but do not quantify the full error rate.
TF-IDF importance is not sentiment or product causality.
The CBOW window and embedding dimension are not fully reported.
BP architecture, loss, seed and stopping rule are not reproducible.
The source claims sentiment accuracy without a frozen test split.
A word-vector model may lose negation, order and sarcasm.
Average sentiment can hide mixed positive and negative sentences.
Correlation screening does not identify causes.
ACF/PACF formulas and table indexing need independent implementation replay.
The difference equations use fitted relationships from the same historical records.
Lag selection and zero-coefficient rules are not sensitivity-tested.
Parameter fits are product-specific and may not transfer to a new launch.
Negative coefficients are interpreted as click farming without direct click data.
Fitted-versus-actual plots are not out-of-sample validation.
PCA standardization removes units but not measurement bias.
Eigenvalue contribution is not a business utility function.
Success-index coefficients are data-dependent and may drift over time.
The top/bottom/all comparison reuses construction data.
Success-index ranges do not establish a calibrated failure probability.
The 5% and 10% sentiment reductions are deterministic stress cases only.
Removing two or four quarters is not rolling-origin validation.
Sensitivity percentages are small but uncertainty intervals are absent.
Product curves may mix review exposure with product quality.
High and low rating findings are observational associations.
“No significant effect” needs sample size and power context.
Negative-review concentration may reflect reporting or selection bias.
Emotional-word rank can reward frequent generic language.
Descriptive adjectives and characteristics are not engineering requirements by themselves.
The memo's design features lack cost, safety and margin analysis.
The recommendation to increase yield needs an operational definition and measurement plan.
“Above average” success-index tracking lacks a calibrated intervention threshold.
The company letter compresses evidence and can sound more certain than the body.
Memo bullets do not establish customer conversion or retention effects.
The 2010-2015 horizon may not represent the current platform.
Appendix tables preserve numbers but not the raw review corpus.
References and tables are evidence sources, not reusable prose.
Watermarks and QR furniture must never become language evidence.
The source page label and PDF page index differ by one after the Summary Sheet.
OCR-like text on scanned pages is incomplete; visual coordinates remain authoritative.
Small formula signs and decimal points require raster confirmation.
Figure legends and appendix column labels can be confused with narrative claims.
A model overview figure does not guarantee executable handoffs.
The BP network's “accurate” claim needs a held-out benchmark.
Difference-equation residual behavior is not reported in a full diagnostic set.
PCA component sign conventions can flip without changing fit but can change prose interpretation.
The same five indicators are reused across products without a measurement-invariance check.
Product-specific weights and coefficients are not accompanied by confidence intervals.
External environment and platform algorithms may drive the observed decline.
Sentiment review count and word count may be missing-not-at-random.
The success index should be monitored with a versioned refit rule.
New product launch advice needs a prospective observation window.
A keyword list is not a complete design requirements document.
The letter's March 2020 date bounds its operational context.
Appendix A positive words and Appendix B top words are not a validated lexicon.
ACF/PACF appendix tables need variable-order checks before reuse.
A small perturbation result cannot support a general robustness claim.
Reusable prose must preserve the source's asymmetric findings and explicit unresolved weaknesses.

Negative-review concentration may reflect reporting or selection bias.
Emotional-word rank can reward frequent generic language.
Descriptive adjectives and characteristics are not engineering requirements by themselves.
The memo's design features lack cost, safety and margin analysis.
The recommendation to increase yield needs an operational definition and measurement plan.
“Above average” success-index tracking lacks a calibrated intervention threshold.
The company letter compresses evidence and can sound more certain than the body.
Memo bullets do not establish customer conversion or retention effects.
The 2010-2015 horizon may not represent the current platform.
Appendix tables preserve numbers but not the raw review corpus.
References and tables are evidence sources, not reusable prose.
Watermarks and QR furniture must never become language evidence.
The source page label and PDF page index differ by one after the Summary Sheet.
OCR-like text on scanned pages is incomplete; visual coordinates remain authoritative.
Small formula signs and decimal points require raster confirmation.
Figure legends and appendix column labels can be confused with narrative claims.
A model overview figure does not guarantee executable handoffs.
The BP network's “accurate” claim needs a held-out benchmark.
Difference-equation residual behavior is not reported in a full diagnostic set.
PCA component sign conventions can flip without changing fit but can change prose interpretation.
The same five indicators are reused across products without a measurement-invariance check.
Product-specific weights and coefficients are not accompanied by confidence intervals.
External environment and platform algorithms may drive the observed decline.
Sentiment review count and word count may be missing-not-at-random.
The success index should be monitored with a versioned refit rule.
New product launch advice needs a prospective observation window.
A keyword list is not a complete design requirements document.
The letter's March 2020 date bounds its operational context.
Appendix A positive words and Appendix B top words are not a validated lexicon.
ACF/PACF appendix tables need variable-order checks before reuse.
A small perturbation result cannot support a general robustness claim.
Reusable prose must preserve the source's asymmetric findings and explicit unresolved weaknesses.
